Middle East.headline: Yemen’s Taiz faces deadly siege, as Shabwah death toll rises
Middle East.body: The siege on Taiz has cut humanitarian supplies to the Yemeni city, the United Nations has warned, and left many of its inhabitants without food and other essentials. UN Human Rights Chief Volker Turk said on Tuesday that the Houthis – an armed group also known as Ansar Allah (Arabic for Supporters of God), who have surrounded the city, must immediately allow humanitarian relief to enter or risk a catastrophe.

Middle East.headline: Yemen displacement tops 250K as Houthis tighten siege on Taiz: What to know
Middle East.body: Yemen displacement tops 250K as Houthis tighten siege on Taiz: What to know The Houthis are looking to completely seize Taiz city, with clashes escalating in other parts of the south as well. The United Nations said Tuesday that more than 250,000 people have been displaced by the recent fighting in Yemen, as the Houthis escalate efforts to defeat government forces in war-torn Taiz and strike deep inside Saudi Arabia. The UN’s refugee agency, UNHCR, said that the number of those displaced between the start of August and Oct. 17 has exceeded 250,000. Africa.headline: Drone attacks across Sudan escalate, 160 people reported killed
Africa.body: By Al Jazeera Staff, AFP and AP Tuesday October 20, 2026 A wave of drone attacks across Sudan has killed more than 160 people in recent days, according to medics and rights groups. Drone attacks on the capital, Khartoum, killed three children on Monday, according to Emergency Lawyers, a group that monitors violence against civilians in Sudan’s civil war, while more than 160 were reported to have been killed in western regions since Friday. The attacks were blamed on the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and government troops, who have been fighting since 2023. Europe.headline: Russian Attacks Hit Energy Facilities Across Western Ukraine, Triggering Blackouts
Europe.body: Russia has widened its attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure to western regions previously spared such strikes, triggering power outages across the country, Ukrainian officials said on Tuesday. The renewed assault began in October, ahead of the cold season, with Russian forces targeting power plants and electricity transmission systems. “Unfortunately, the enemy continues to deliberately and systematically attack our energy infrastructure,” Deputy Energy Minister Artem Nekrasov said in a televised statement. Asia-Pacific.headline: Guterres warns global food system still faces hunger and food insecurity crisis
Asia-Pacific.body: United Nations Secretary-General Antonio Guterres has warned that hunger remains at an unacceptable level around the world and stressed the need for practical action to ensure access to safe and sufficient food for all people. In a post on his social media account on Monday, Oct. 27, he said that despite progress in recent decades, the global food system still faces serious challenges. Reiterating the inherent right of all people to access food, Guterres called on countries to turn their commitments into practical steps and to provide sustainable, healthy and fair food systems. Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: Central and West Africa — Rare Ebola strain spreads as regional death toll exceeds 4,400
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: An ongoing outbreak of the rare Bundibugyo Ebola virus strain, which lacks an approved vaccine or targeted cure, has caused at least 4,478 deaths among 9,277 confirmed cases since May, predominantly in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Ituri province is the most severely affected area, accounting for over 6,800 cases. Nigeria became the fifth country affected after confirming an imported case in an isolated patient in Abuja who traveled from eastern DRC through Uganda. Nigerian authorities are conducting contact tracing for 44 exposed individuals and intensifying screening at airports. Health officials in Uganda report no active confirmed cases remaining in the country.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: France and Spain — Flash floods and landslides from Storm Adam leave six dead
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: Torrential rain and severe flash flooding triggered by Storm Adam have resulted in six confirmed fatalities across southwestern Europe, with five deaths in Spain and one in southern France. Overflowing rivers submerged roads and inundated numerous homes, while landslides caused severe structural damage to buildings. Emergency authorities in both countries have executed mass evacuations in affected communities as emergency operations continue.
